# Stima Prova · The post-AI skill assessment

Source: https://mystima.io/

Stima Prova · The post-AI skill assessment

## Work with the machine. Prove the human.

Stima Prova turns the assignment or take-home you already use into an AI-allowed session, grading the work on your rubric and the AI use on a published scale, every score cited to the record.

- Free for instructors
- From $29 per assessment for teams
- 14-day free trial for teams

- The work, on your criteria: The deliverable is graded blind on your rubric, separate from the process.
- Every score cited: Each score points to a moment in the recorded session. Check the reasoning in one click.
- How you worked: Graded on the published Delegator, Operator, Director scale, read against what the task needed.

The problem

### Everyone already works with AI. Almost nothing measures how.

The polished submission used to be the signal. In a post-AI world, the signal moved into the process, where nobody can see it.

83%

#### Candidates would use AI if allowed

And 14% admit they already do. Banning it doesn't remove AI from the take-home; it just removes it from your view.

HACKERRANK CANDIDATE RESEARCH

66%

#### Leaders won't hire without AI skills

The requirement is universal, the standard doesn't exist, so every interviewer improvises their own probe, and transcripts say nothing.

61%

#### False positives from AI detectors

Of essays by non-native English writers, falsely flagged as AI-written. Detection punishes the wrong people and explains nothing.

STANFORD, LIANG ET AL., PATTERNS 2023

The result: people learn to hide AI use, not to use it well.

How it works

### From the work you already use to graded evidence.

01

#### Adapt

Bring one assignment or role question. We reshape it with you, same goals, same rubric, plus a planted difficulty a blind copy-paste gets wrong.

02

#### Session

The person works one focused, timed session with AI explicitly allowed, recorded with consent. No video recording. No lockdown browser.

03

#### Two scores

The work, graded on your rubric. The process, graded on a published scale. Every score cites a moment in the session record.

04

#### Confirm

A human confirms every outcome before it counts. Grades and decisions export as CSV for your LMS or ATS, with a paper trail you can defend.

The AI-collaboration scale

### Three levels. Higher is not better.

The scale reads how much thinking was handed to the model, prompts, edits, verification, model switching, time. The grade is calibration: the observed level against what the task demanded.

Pick a task · the right level changes

- Summarize a long meeting transcript: Delegator. Model-strong and low-stakes, and a quick skim verifies it. Handing it over is exactly right.
- Clean a messy CSV to spec: Operator. Verifiable and routine, but the spec has teeth. Iterate against the requirements and spot-check the output.
- Reply to an angry enterprise customer: Director. High stakes with deep company context. Someone must set the approach, verify what matters, and own the result.

Level 1

#### Delegator

Hands work to AI

Restates the brief, accepts the first answer. Right for verifiable, low-stakes work.

Level 2

#### Operator

Works with AI

Iterates, corrects, edits substantively. The right default for mixed, everyday work.

Level 3

#### Director

Leads the work

Sets the approach first, verifies the parts most likely wrong, owns the outcome.

- Calibrated, matched the task
- Near · one step off
- Under-directed · handed off judgment
- Over-directed · controlled what AI could carry

Trust & privacy

### No proctoring. No prohibition. No black boxes.

#### Consent-first recording

Workspace-only. No video recording, no keystroke logging, no lockdown browser. Participants see exactly what is kept before they start.

#### Humans confirm outcomes

Every outcome is confirmed by a person. Low-confidence results route to a reviewer, and participants can dispute.

#### Your rubric stays yours

Your criteria grade the work; the collaboration scale is added alongside, never instead. Results stay comparable across courses and roles.

#### Data handling with care

FERPA-aligned for campuses, hosted in the EU, DPA on request, no training on your data. Built to WCAG 2.1 AA.

What you get, per candidate

### A decision you can defend. Not a feeling.

#### Quality of the work

A 0–100 score on the finished deliverable, graded blind on your criteria, with the rubric beside it.

#### AI collaboration level

Delegator, Operator, or Director, read against what the task needed. This task needed a Director, and the session showed one.

#### Every claim cites the tape

Each score points to a moment in the recorded session, so anyone on your team can check the reasoning in one click.

#### Risk flags sit beside the grade

Unverified acceptance on high-stakes work and the blind pass get flagged, even when the numbers look fine. Compliance gets artifacts, not assurances.

#### Candidates get a fairer process

Shorter, AI-allowed, with a verified result they own and can share. You get the paper trail.

Trust & compliance

### The detection arms race ends by stepping out of it.

#### AI-allowed by design

Nothing to police, nothing to ban. The question moves from "did they use it" to "how well did they use it."

#### Consent-first recording

No video or audio recording, no keystroke logging. Candidates see exactly what is kept before they agree.

#### Humans confirm outcomes

Low-confidence results route to your team, and every outcome is confirmed by a person before it counts.

#### Ready for audit

Every decision has a documented reason. EU hosting on every plan, DPA on request.

The problem

### Every professor improvises a policy. Grades score the essay, not the learning.

Applying an AI policy means redesigning assignments course by course. Departments don't have the staff, so the document says one thing and every classroom does another.

What students leave with

### A grade for the course. Proof for the career.

#### Feedback pointers

After every assignment, students see in plain language where they delegated blindly and where a check would have caught an error. Responsible AI use is taught, not just demanded.

#### A verified AI-competency result

Each assignment produces a verifiable credential (Open Badges 3.0) and a shareable result page, dated and explained. Real evidence behind the "AI skills" line on a résumé.

#### Levels that grow with them

Measured again in every course on the same scale, from Delegator to Operator to Director. Growth becomes visible across a degree, and the university's output becomes readable from the outside.

Built for the classroom

# Assessment After AI: Free Position Paper on Post-AI Assessment | Stima

Source: https://mystima.io/paper

Stima Prova · Position Paper No. 01 · Free

## Assessment After AI.

Why banning AI from assessment tests a world that no longer exists, what to measure instead, and how a credential survives when any answer can be generated. Nine pages. No buzzwords.

- PDF · 9 pages
- Free with your email

### Inside the paper.

01

#### The why

The exam tested a world that has ended. When any answer can be generated, answers stop being evidence. Judgment becomes the evidence.

02

#### The false binary

Ban it, or surrender to it. Why both are the same mistake, dressed in opposite colors.

03

#### The philosophy

Direction, judgment, ownership: the three dimensions a post-AI assessment has to score.

04

#### The moat

A prompt can write a task. It cannot write a measurement. What it actually takes to build one.

05

#### In practice

The audit brief: a worked example of an assessment where the machine is in the room, on purpose.

06

#### Principles

Eight rules we build by.

"The task is now free. The measurement is the product."

Assessment After AI · Section 04
